newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares record gains, long holidays ahead.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares record gains, long holidays ahead.

text.p: Blue-chips posted small gains on short-covering at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, the last day of trade in the current settlement, dealers said.
"Gains in blue-chip stocks were mostly due to short-covering by speculators," a trader said. "The undertone remains weak."
The benchmark BSE 30-share index rose 22.50 points, or 0.74 percent, to 3,066.66 off 3,073.61. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) index was up 8.32 points to 874.89.
The BSE is closed on Friday, Monday and Tuesday for the Hindu New Year. It will open briefly for an auspicious "moorat" session on Sunday to herald the New Year.
Traders said lack of any market moving news kept prices in a narrow band, with speculative action seen in pivotal stocks.

Shares of tobacco giant ITC which were hammered nearly 15 percent in the last two days on the BSE rose on short-covering. ITC was up 9.0 rupees, or 3.69 prcent, to 253.0 rupees, but lost 5.95 rupees to close at 249.60 on the NSE.
The firm, India's biggest cigarette company, is being investigated by a federal agency for alleged foreign exchange violations to the tune of over $100 million.
Reliance gained 0.50 rupees to 185.50 rupees, TISCO 0.25 to 166, ITC 9.0 to 253.0, Bajaj Auto 18.70 to 929.25, L&T 4.50 to 220.0, ACC 15.20 to 1,433.25 and Hind Lever 4.0 to 781.25.
SBI lost 1.25 to 212.75 and ICICI 0.50 to 57.50.
Shares of state-run Hindustan Petroleum rose 0.75 to 317.25 in volumes of 6,800 shares traded at the BSE ahead of the firm's board meeting discuss first half 1996/97 results.
HPCL officials told Reuters the company was not likely to announce its results before Friday morning. The firm's meeting started at 1700 hours (1130 GMT) on Thursday.
